That distinction decides the whole item: an unenforced typecheck does not stop a foreign error from reaching operator-vite's ratchet, so the attribution defect would survive its own fix. Merit left UNTRIAGED for exactly that reason rather than guessed in either direction.

evidence.notes: PREMISE VERIFIED AND THE DEFECT IS LARGER THAN FILED. The item reports that sibling work-items can share one payload.plan_item stamp, so completing a SUB-LANE child flips its PARENT's plan item to done via finishPlanStamp(), and states 126 plan items affected with 51 still live. Measured 2026-08-22 over harness_shared.work_items in papercusp-workspace: 4,602 stamped rows across 4,337 distinct (plan_slug,item_id) stamps, of which 200 stamps are SHARED by more than one row, spanning 465 rows, and 83 of those shared stamps still have at least one live (non-done/dropped/deprecated) sibling. So the true figures are 200 affected stamps (filed: 126) and 83 with a live sibling (filed: 51) — the filer UNDER-CLAIMED by ~1.6x on both. That is the THIRD independent confirmation of D-026 s4's direction-of-error rule, on a third unrelated finding, and it is now safe to treat "a filed number is a floor to re-measure" as established rather than suggestive. R-related to EI-20577421906951067, not a duplicate: this one is the OVER-FIRE (things get closed that should not be), that one is the IRREVERSIBILITY (a wrong closure cannot be undone). They are two halves of one trap and neither is safe to fix alone — fixing only the over-fire leaves existing bad closures stuck; fixing only the reopen path leaves the source of them running. Both are complaints against the very reconciler whose existence supersedes EI-2443/EI-2725 in this same batch.
